newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: African states shun immigrants ejected by Spain.
newsitem.headline: African states shun immigrants ejected by Spain.

text.p: Six African countries have refused to accept 45 African immigrants deported by Spain in June and now jailed in the West African state of Guinea-Bissau, officials said on Tuesday.

A Guinea-Bissau interior ministry source told the Portuguese news agency Lusa that Nigeria, Liberia, Central African Republic, Cameroon, Togo and Rwanda had informed Guinea-Bissau they would not take the men who say they come from those states.
"Bissau will have to resolve the problem directly with Madrid," said the source, who asked not to be identified.

"No one wants these men because they are carrying no identification papers," Leopoldo Amado, spokesman for the Guinea-Bissau League for Human Rights, told Reuters in a telephone interview from the former Portuguese colony.
The group are among hundreds of Africans who try to cross the narrow Strait of Gibraltar into Spain from north Africa every year in search of a better life in Europe.

Amado said the expulsion of the Africans to Guinea-Bissau was illegal because some had previusly filled in papers at a centre for immigrants in the Spain's North African enclave of Melilla, requesting travel to Spain.
He said the authorities had repatriated just five of the original group of 50 to neighbouring Guinea so far.
Spanish authorities had bribed the Guinea-Bissau government to take the immigrants after Senegal and Cameroon had turned them away, Amado said.
The Africans staged two brief hunger strikes last month to press for their return to Spain, he added.
Bissau police used truncheons, plastic bullets and tear gas to disperse the Africans at a protest in front of the interior ministry on Monday, injuring one immigrant.
Police were now holding the men in cramped conditions in a cell in Bissau, Amado said. "They live in subhuman conditions," he added.
